chapter: Bennie Moten, Basie and the Reno
title: Introducing Bennie Moten and Lovett's pool games with him
summary: Smith turns to Moten; Lovett sat in with his band but was with George Lee then, and played pool with Moten.

bands.name: Art Smith Kansas City Jazz Band

story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: We were talking about Bunk Johnson. I think the interesting thing was that Baby and Bunk played together here in Kansas City rather than down in New Orleans. Now I think I would like to get on to one of the really truly famous, best known, Kansas City jazz musicians -- people might think of Count Basie when I say that but really I'm talking about Benny Moten, Benny Moten "Moten" Swing, and there's so much to tell about him.
I think there are things that can be told on this tape that are not in books that I learned when I came out here in 1962, organized my band and traveled with my band. I

personally used to buy Benny Moten records when I was 14, 15 years of age, the old 78s. Booker T. Washington was featured on trumpet with that band and he's now with the Art Smith Kansas City Jazz Band. I would have bet you a million to one against that ever happening when I was a boy back home in Boston, but now I'd like to talk about Benny Moten.

I'd like somebody to tell us about when the band was in Denver and when Benny came back, had that tonsillectomy done by the surgeon here and what happened but anyway, let's start out with Benny Moten; what kind of a man he was, what kind of a band leader and musician and what your personal feelings were about the great Benny Moten. Baby, did you ever play for Benny Moten?
Oh, I've sit in his band. I've sit in. I never played with him. I never played with Benny Moten's band. I was with George Lee's band during the time Benny was famous around here.
Well you must have known him?
Oh yes, I knew Benny well, I know him well. We used to play pool together.
Was he a good pool player?
